howto.name: Upload the base PDF
howto.text: The main document (A). The output keeps its pages, bookmarks, links and form fields.

howto.name: Upload the overlay PDF
howto.text: The PDF (B) whose pages are layered onto the base, on top of it or behind it depending on the mode.

howto.name: Choose mode and download
howto.text: Overlay puts B on top of A; Stamp puts B behind A as a background. Output: the base PDF with an overlay page drawn onto each of its pages.

faq.q: What's the difference between overlay and merge?
faq.a: Merge concatenates files page-by-page. Overlay composites pages on top of each other — useful for adding letterheads, watermarks-from-PDF, or repeating templates.

faq.q: Can I overlay only some pages?
faq.a: No. Every base page gets an overlay page: overlay page 1 goes on base page 1, page 2 on page 2, and so on, and once the overlay runs out its first page is reused for the remaining base pages. A one-page overlay, such as a letterhead, therefore lands on every page.
Yes — PDF supports transparency and the overlay's alpha is honored. White rectangles still cover what's beneath; transparent regions show base content through.
